messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 page — BorealisCorp (private VPC) NLB healthchecks failing in eu-west-1 for tenant=borealis. Created INC-20260301-4123. Pager oncall(sre-oncall).

sre-oncall: Ack, I'm on it. Jumping into the bridge and grabbing target group + NLB state.

netops-liz: Looking at NLB target group tgborealis-01 — ~60% of targets unhealthy, healthcheck failures: TCP healthcheck timeout / connection reset. Backend instances showing lots of ESTABLISHED -> TIME_WAIT -> RST churn in system logs.

eng-runtime-max: Confirmed from runtime telemetry: request success rate dropped ~40% for that tenant, p50 latency unchanged for healthy nodes. No code deploys in the last 2 hours.

netops-liz: Quick check of NAT/egress instance for tenant shows conntrack table near capacity (conntrack: 65530/65536). Likely NAT instance is dropping new connections -> NLB healthchecks failing when they try new connections.

oncall-yusuf: If conntrack is the culprit, tuned conntrack or scaling NAT is quicker than touching customer DNS. What's the player risk if we increase conntrack?

netops-liz: We'll need to either increase conntrack max and reboot the NAT (risky) or move tenant traffic off the affected NAT (safer). Can we shift traffic to the fallback ALB in the same VPC?

eng-sre-pager: Verified backup ALB (alb-borealis-02) is healthy and has spare capacity. Route53 has weighted record for borealis-api with 90/10 primary/backup.

solutions-jen: I can message the customer lead Maria (customer-borealis-maria) to say we may perform a controlled traffic shift; they requested minimal downtime. Maria: are you ok with a brief maintenance window or prefer transparent failover? @maria

customer-borealis-maria: We cannot have downtime >30s; prefer transparent failover. Please keep us updated in the bridge.

sre-oncall: Plan: 1) perform conservative conntrack tuning on NAT (#1) to buy time (increase nf_conntrack_max + tune timeouts) 2) if health doesn't recover in 3m, shift Route53 weight to backup ALB 100% (transparent) 3) isolate tenant NAT and scale out or replace.

netops-liz: Executing step 1 now: applying sysctl on nat-tenant-1 (one at a time):

```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400
```

netops-liz: Conntrack count dropped from 65530 -> 4100 after removing stale entries and increasing table. Healthchecks started recovering on a subset of targets.

eng-runtime-max: Runtime shows gradual recovery, success rate climbing back to ~92% for requests routed to repaired nodes. Still a few unhealthy targets.

oncall-yusuf: Recommend we still prepare DNS weight flip as fallback. I can pre-run the Route53 change but not commit until we agree.

sre-oncall: Agreed. Prepare change but hold. Creating incident bridge and runbook links: bridge: https://meet.redwood/INC-20260301-4123 bridge | runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nlb-healthcheck

incident-bot: Incident bridge created by sre-oncall.

netops-liz: After conntrack tuning, new connections ok, but one NAT instance still shows flapping conntrack counts -> plan to cordon that NAT and replace with nat-tenant-2 (cold). Scheduling replacement now; traffic will shift away gradually.

eng-sre-pager: Observability: ALB fallback remains <5% weight, can accept 100% if needed. No change in rate-limited quotas for tenant.

solutions-jen: Notifying Borealis on the bridge and Slack: "We are seeing transient NAT connection exhaustion causing NLB healthchecks to fail. We applied temporary conntrack tuning and are replacing the flapping NAT instance. If health doesn't stabilize in 3m we'll perform a transparent DNS weight shift to backup ALB."

customer-borealis-maria: Received. Please proceed, keep within the 30s downtime constraint.

sre-oncall: Health stable across 95% of targets after NAT replacement started, p95 latency ok. Holding off DNS change. Monitoring for 30m.

netops-liz: Running post-fix validation: curl to NLB endpoint shows 200 on all healthy targets. No more TCP RSTs on backend.

eng-runtime-max: Telemetry: error budget burn stopped. Feature checks ok.

oncall-yusuf: Good cleanup items: 1) revert aggressive conntrack timeouts after stable 24h 2) add alert on conntrack utilization for tenant NATs 3) postmortem + customer impact note.

solutions-jen: I'll draft the customer-facing incident summary and CS will send within 1 hour.

sre-oncall: Incident state: mitigation complete :white_check_mark:. Services healthy, monitoring for 30m. Assigning postmortem to netops-liz + eng-runtime-max. Tagging runbook follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260301-4123 moved to MONITORING.

eng-sre-pager: Adding owners: Netops-Liz (exec) and EngRuntime-Max (tech lead).

sre-oncall: Thanks team — closing the active paging loop. Postmortem owner will publish notes in #postmortems within 72h.

customer-borealis-maria: Thanks for the quick response. Appreciate the updates.

netops-liz: Filing follow-up task to increase conntrack headroom across tenant NAT fleet and add automated replacement on conntrack OOM.

sre-oncall: End of thread.
